1) positional goods are a subset economic goods whose consumption depends negatively on consumption others; 2) the consumption of positional goods, hence, is subject to the law of diminishing marginal utility; 3) the consumption of a positional good is, thus, a Giffen good; 4) the consumption of such a good is, thus subject to the law Giffen goods and is subject to a Giffen paradox.
the consumption of positional goods can be explained by the same economic theory that explains the consumption of standard private and public goods, but with a different institutional context.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the institutional microeconomics of positional good, is a microeconomic foundation for a theory of institutional economics of positional good, i.e. the institutional microeconmics of positional goods.
the institutional economics of positional good is a subset of institutional economics of public good.
the institutional concerns are the following: 1) the positional goods are the result of a social construction, and 2) the positional good can only be defined by a social construction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the institutional design of a society has to take into account the existence of positional goods.

the market for positional goods is a market for a positional good, and hence is a market for an economic good with a double rival and double exclusion characteristics, i.e. a market for a double rival good, which is not a textbook economic good, but a positional good.
positional goods are a particular case of double rival goods, and hence, the institutional economics literature can be used to study them.
